title: Supio vs Eve Legal vs Codes Health
summary: Compare Supio, Eve Legal, and Codes Health for plaintiff law firms. See how AI-powered medical record retrieval stacks up against demand-drafting, chronology, and full-lifecycle litigation platforms.
body_text: Plaintiff law firms face a fundamental workflow problem: you cannot analyze medical records you do not have. While AI-powered legal platforms promise faster case preparation and higher settlement values, the critical question is whether these tools solve the actual bottleneck slowing your cases. This comparison examines three platforms, Supio, Eve Legal, and Codes Health , to help litigation teams understand which solution addresses their specific pre-litigation and case-preparation challenges. Key Takeaways Among these three platforms, Codes Health is the only one that clearly combines medical record retrieval with AI-powered analysis in a single platform. Supio and Eve Legal emphasize analysis, drafting, and litigation workflows rather than full retrieval, so firms using them still need to solve retrieval elsewhere. Record retrieval remains a common root cause of case delays. Traditional retrieval can take weeks or months, depending on provider responsiveness. Codes Health delivers complete records in a couple of weeks, which addresses that bottleneck directly. Codes Health explicitly markets human-verified AI insights, with medical and legal experts reviewing outputs before delivery. Codes Health combines missing-record detection with the retrieval process itself, flagging documentation gaps before trial preparation begins. Vendors that promise same-day retrieval often can't guarantee complete records, which pushes the client and firm back into the process to track down what's missing, a pattern that contributes to churn. Codes Health prioritizes complete records over shortcuts on speed. Eve Legal appears to offer the broadest single-platform workflow among the three, spanning intake through discovery. Supio provides a direct Westlaw integration for citation validation. Codes Health solves the retrieval-to-insight pipeline that neither competitor addresses. The Legal AI Landscape: Why Your Retrieval Strategy Matters The plaintiff legal tech market has expanded rapidly, with platforms promising to reduce the manual burden of medical record review, demand letter generation, and case chronology creation. However, a critical assumption underlies most of these tools: that your firm already has complete, timely access to the medical records needed for analysis. That assumption creates a real gap for many practices. Traditional retrieval can stretch across weeks or months, and incomplete authorizations can send requests back to the start. When that happens, the speed of your AI analysis stops mattering, because your cases stall at the retrieval stage, not the analysis stage. Common Pre-Litigation Bottlenecks Law firms handling personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, and workers' compensation cases frequently run into these workflow problems: Incomplete authorizations : Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records cause provider rejections and add real delay to an already lengthy federal timeline Multiple provider coordination : Complex injury cases often involve nine or ten different treatment facilities, each requiring independent tracking and follow-up Missing record gaps : Records that appear complete may still lack critical documentation from specialists, imaging centers, or pharmacy records Manual review burden : Attorneys and paralegals spend hours reviewing thousands of pages to identify relevant diagnoses, treatments, and breach-of-care indicators Vendor fragmentation : Coordinating between retrieval services, record review vendors, and case management systems creates accountability gaps Understanding which platform addresses these specific bottlenecks, rather than which offers the longest feature list, is what actually determines the value each provides to your practice. Head-to-Head: Supio vs Eve Legal vs Codes Health Medical Record Retrieval This capability represents the most significant functional difference between the three platforms. Codes Health : Offers a full retrieval service through a mix of digital connections, including claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, and proprietary provider networks, alongside traditional fax outreach. Complete records typically arrive in a couple of weeks. Supio : Based on its official materials, Supio emphasizes analysis and drafting rather than full medical-record retrieval, so firms typically need a separate retrieval vendor. Eve Legal : Similarly focused on intake, casework, and discovery workflows rather than retrieval, so firms typically need a separate retrieval vendor here too. Codes Health also uses proprietary databases to help locate patients' previous providers, which is particularly valuable for cases involving multiple treatment facilities or years of medical history. For firms using Supio or Eve Legal, that generally means maintaining a separate retrieval vendor relationship, coordinating handoffs between systems, and managing accountability when records arrive late or incomplete. AI-Powered Medical Chronologies All three platforms offer AI-generated medical chronologies, though with different approaches to quality assurance: Codes Health: Automatically organizes records into chronological order Groups all patient encounters and bills by visit Identifies missing records within the timeline Delivers human-verified outputs before final delivery Supio: Markets fast, AI-generated medical chronologies Institutional memory that learns from a firm's case history Says its chronology tool can spot gaps and missing documents Eve Legal: Markets AI-native workflows that automate intake, drafting, research, and discovery-related work Offers broad workflow coverage from intake through discovery AI-driven automation across multiple case stages Where General AI Tools Fall Short General AI platforms like ChatGPT aren't built to accurately analyze medical records. They don't have the structure to reliably parse dense clinical documentation, catch buried diagnoses, or build a chronology that can hold up in a legal setting. Codes Health's platform is purpose-built for this specific job, pairing AI extraction with medical and legal expert review so the output can withstand the level of precision litigation actually requires. Non-zero error risk persists in any AI system, which is exactly why that human review step matters. Human Verification and Quality Assurance The reliability of AI outputs in litigation contexts remains a real concern. Error risk persists even in purpose-built legal AI platforms, which is why human oversight matters for defensible work product. Codes Health : Markets human-verified AI insights, with outputs reviewed by medical and legal experts. Supio : Human review options weren't confirmed as tier-specific in the sources reviewed here. Eve Legal : Emphasizes validation and source-checking within its workflow, though the exact review process wasn't confirmed as fully AI-only or human-involved from the sources reviewed. Codes Health positions its hybrid AI-human approach as central to litigation-grade accuracy, with insights validated before delivery to reduce the risk of AI-generated errors appearing in court filings or settlement negotiations. Missing Record Detection Codes Health combines missing-record detection with the retrieval process itself, which is a different positioning from analysis-first tools. Supio's chronology tool also says it can spot gaps and missing documents, so this isn't exclusive to Codes Health, but Codes Health's version is tied directly to retrieval rather than analysis of records already in hand. The platform's Missing Record Review cross-references patient medical history to identify documentation gaps before trial preparation begins. This helps guard against: Trial surprises when opposing counsel surfaces records your team never obtained Incomplete damage calculations, missing specialist visits, or diagnostic imaging Gaps in treatment timelines that weaken causation arguments Settlement negotiations based on incomplete medical pictures Breach-of-Care and Insights Extraction For medical malpractice, personal injury, and wrongful death cases, identifying deviations from medical standards is essential to building liability arguments. Codes Health automatically flags breaches in care, future medical expenses, and case facts such as missed appointments and pre-existing conditions. The insights extraction engine surfaces structured data from unstructured medical records, helping attorneys identify case-critical elements that might otherwise require hours of manual review. Supio offers medical analysis capabilities focused on supporting demand letter generation, with an emphasis on medical-legal standards validation through its Westlaw integration. Eve Legal provides analysis within its broader workflow platform, covering multiple stages of case preparation from intake through discovery. Demand Letter Generation and Discovery Support This is where Supio and Eve Legal offer capabilities that extend beyond Codes Health's primary focus: Eve Legal: Discovery support spanning intake through trial preparation A nightly AI Auditor that scans caseloads for missed value Legal research covering case law, statutes, and regulations across jurisdictions Intake capability across dozens of languages Supio: A direct Westlaw Advantage partnership for citation validation 24/7 voice intake capabilities CaseAware AI for cross-case intelligence and pattern recognition Institutional memory that compounds with every case Codes Health: Primary focus on retrieval and medical analysis Supports litigation preparation through verified medical insights Built to solve the retrieval bottleneck first Firms with established demand letter workflows may find Supio or Eve Legal valuable additions. Firms whose primary bottleneck is obtaining complete records in time to use those tools will benefit from addressing retrieval first. Integration Ecosystems Compared Record Access Channels Codes Health : Direct connections across claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, and proprietary provider networks, alongside traditional fax outreach. Supio : Not positioned around direct record-access channels in its official materials. Eve Legal : Not positioned around direct record-access channels in its official materials. Codes Health's multi-channel access to provider networks helps it retrieve records without relying solely on traditional fax requests, which is part of why its typical turnaround runs to a couple of weeks rather than longer. Case Management System Integration All three platforms offer case management integrations, though with different emphasis: Codes Health : Can build custom integrations for high-volume customers with CRM platforms and medical software. Supio : Multiple case management system integrations, including Litify, MyCase, CasePeer, and Filevine. Eve Legal : A Clio Manage bidirectional sync, plus additional case management connections. Legal Research Integration Supio maintains a direct Thomson Reuters Westlaw Advantage partnership, the only platform among the three with this specific research integration, enabling citation validation against the legal content judges actually use. Eve Legal offers built-in legal research covering case law, statutes, and regulations across jurisdictions, though not through the same Westlaw partnership. Codes Health focuses on medical-legal standards rather than general legal research, positioning the platform as a specialized tool for the record retrieval and medical analysis phase rather than a comprehensive litigation platform. Authorization Quality: The Hidden Cause of Retrieval Delays One often-overlooked factor in retrieval speed is authorization quality. Incomplete authorizations are a leading cause of denied requests. Common issues include: Missing or illegible patient signatures Unclear expiration dates Unchecked boxes for sensitive record categories (mental health, substance abuse, HIV) Misspellings of patient names or provider names Missing dates of service Each rejection adds delay to an already lengthy process, since medical record requests generally fall under a 30-day federal turnaround standard under HIPAA, with some state rules varying. A rejection just means starting that clock over. Codes Health addresses this through proactive AI error checking that reviews authorization forms before submission. The system automatically flags common rejection causes, including misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature problems, before they reach providers. This pre-submission verification isn't something Supio or Eve Legal offers, since both platforms assume records are obtained through separate channels. Best Fit Scenarios: Which Platform Solves Your Problem? Choose Codes Health When: Your primary bottleneck is record retrieval speed and completeness You need end-to-end retrieval and analysis in a single relationship Trial-ready completeness matters, and missing-record detection would help You require human-verified AI outputs reviewed by medical experts Vendor consolidation is a priority for your firm Choose Supio When: You already have reliable record retrieval solved, and your bottleneck is analysis Westlaw-validated outputs are important for citation verification You want a platform that builds institutional memory over time 24/7 intake capability would help with after-hours lead qualification Choose Eve Legal When: You need a single comprehensive platform spanning intake through discovery Nightly caseload auditing for missed value matters to your practice Built-in legal research across jurisdictions is a priority Multi-language intake is important for your client base You want broad workflow automation across multiple case stages Hybrid Approaches Firms with different pain points may benefit from combining platforms: Codes Health with Supio : Use Codes Health for retrieval and initial analysis, Supio for demand letter generation with Westlaw validation. Codes Health with Eve Legal : Use Codes Health to solve the retrieval bottleneck, Eve Legal for broader discovery and intake workflows. The decision depends on which bottleneck most significantly impacts your case timelines and settlement outcomes. Performance and ROI Considerations Codes Health reports client gains such as reduced manual review time, faster chronology creation, higher case capacity, and larger settlements. These are vendor-reported outcomes, and results may vary by firm and case type. As with any legal AI platform, independent third-party validation of these kinds of metrics is still limited across the industry, so it's worth asking any vendor, including Codes Health, how their figures were measured. Total Cost of Ownership Direct pricing comparisons are difficult because none of the three platforms publish exact public pricing. Codes Health uses a flat fee that includes retrieval. Supio and Eve Legal don't appear to publish pricing on their official sites, and both route prospective customers to a demo or sales call. One structural difference is worth noting: firms using Supio or Eve Legal for analysis typically still need a separate retrieval vendor and its associated costs, while Codes Health bundles retrieval and analysis into a single relationship. Security and Compliance All three platforms state HIPAA compliance, which matters for handling protected health information in legal contexts. HIPAA : All three platforms state compliance. SOC 2 : Supio publicly states SOC 2 certification. Codes Health and Eve Legal's SOC 2 status wasn't confirmed in the sources reviewed here. For firms handling sensitive medical records in litigation, compliance verification should be part of any vendor evaluation process. Switching and Implementation Moving from Traditional Retrieval to Codes Health For firms currently using traditional retrieval services, such as mail or fax-only vendors, switching to Codes Health generally means: Low complexity, since there's no existing digital workflow to displace Minimal risk, since it adds a capability rather than replacing established systems Adding Supio or Eve Legal to Existing Workflows Firms with retrieval already solved may add Supio or Eve Legal for analysis and drafting. This typically involves moderate complexity, since it requires integrating with existing case management systems, along with some template configuration and setup time. Using Multiple Platforms Firms combining Codes Health for retrieval with Supio or Eve Legal for downstream workflows should plan for coordination between platforms, clear data handoff processes, and clear accountability for each stage of case preparation. Conclusion The choice between Supio, Eve Legal, and Codes Health depends on where your firm's cases actually stall. If your bottleneck is obtaining complete medical records, Codes Health addresses that directly with retrieval in a couple of weeks, human-verified AI analysis, and missing-record detection built into the retrieval process, capabilities neither competitor offers in the same way. Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team also continues building out additional workflows and products, so the platform keeps evolving to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices. If you already have reliable retrieval and need demand letter automation or full lifecycle case management, Supio and Eve Legal offer those downstream capabilities. Some firms may benefit from combining platforms to address different stages of case preparation. The fundamental question is whether your cases delay at the retrieval stage or the analysis stage. Solve the actual bottleneck first, then evaluate additional tools. Frequently Asked Questions How does Codes Health's retrieval speed compare to traditional services? Traditional medical record retrieval can take weeks or months, depending on provider responsiveness and authorization quality. Codes Health typically delivers complete records in a couple of weeks through a mix of digital connections and traditional fax outreach. Can I use Codes Health alongside Supio or Eve Legal? Yes. Firms with different bottlenecks often combine platforms. Codes Health addresses the retrieval-to-analysis pipeline, while Supio offers Westlaw-validated demand letters and Eve Legal provides broader workflow coverage. The decision depends on which stages of your case preparation create the most friction. What happens if AI makes an error in case analysis? Error risk persists in any AI system, including general-purpose tools like ChatGPT, which aren't built for litigation-grade medical analysis in the first place. Codes Health addresses this by verifying outputs with medical and legal experts before delivery. Attorney review remains essential regardless of platform. Does Codes Health work for mass tort cases with multiple claimants? Yes. Codes Health's secure document storage enables record reuse across multiple cases or care episodes without repeated retrieval costs. For mass tort practices handling multiple claims for individual plaintiffs, this reduces redundant requests and the delays that come with them. How does Missing Record Detection work? Codes Health's Missing Record Review cross-references patient medical history to identify gaps in documentation before trial preparation. The system compares obtained records against expected treatment patterns, specialist referrals, and diagnostic sequences to flag potential missing documents, helping prevent trial surprises when opposing counsel surfaces records your team never requested.

title: Flip accelerates global expansion with strategic partnership in the UK
summary: Flip, the Super App for frontline employees, joins forces with Work Networks.
body_text: LONDON, November 22 2024 – Flip , Europe’s leading frontline employee super-app, today announced a partnership with Work Networks in the UK. This news follows Flip’s recent collaboration with Enablo , a provider of cutting-edge communication and productivity solutions, marking another pivotal step in the company’s global growth strategy. This partnership further Flip’s mission to transform the employee experience for deskless and frontline workforces worldwide. Global Presence, Local Expertise In the UK, Flip’s partnership with Work Networks, a pioneering digital transformation firm and one of the first Workplace by Meta partners, unites Flip’s powerful frontline employee platform with extensive regional expertise in complex enterprise transitions. With a client portfolio that includes organisations like Danone, AstraZeneca, the World Health Organization (WHO) and the National Health Service (NHS), Work Networks shares Flip’s commitment to creating significant organisational impact through technology and cultural transformation. Experienced Partners for Workplace by Meta Transitions “Moving a large, diverse workforce to a new communication platform can be risky, especially to employee engagement and adoption,” says Benedikt Brand (né Ilg), CEO of Flip. “Our partnerships with Work Networks brings localised expertise to help guide large organisations successfully through this transition. Worknetworks knows Workplace’s ecosystems inside and out, and they chose Flip because they see us as the ideal solution for former Workplace customers. Together, we’re delivering a powerful, next-level platform that strengthens internal communication and operational efficiency for businesses worldwide” With Flip’s intuitive interface and robust functionalities, frontline workers across sectors, from retail to manufacturing, can streamline communication, manage HR tasks, and foster stronger team connections—all in one platform. Nick Crawford, CEO, at Work Networks, says “Our collaboration with Flip is an exciting opportunity to redefine how organisations connect with their frontline employees in the UK. Having been at the forefront of Workplace from Meta, we understand that successful transitions require more than technology; they demand a strategic focus on employee engagement and support. Together with Flip, we're driving a cultural shift that enables companies to cultivate strong connections and foster a truly inclusive digital workplace.” These partnerships come on the heels of Flip’s recent acquisition of The Bot Platform and two key appointments from Workplace by Meta. Flip is trusted by over 400 global companies, including Bosch, McDonald’s Germany, Rossmann and Porsche to reach, engage, and transform their frontline workforces. About Flip Flip is the employee experience platform that’s transforming the day-to-day of deskless workforces across the globe. Its white-label app creates a single point of contact between businesses and their frontline employees, bundling internal communications and HR tools into one easy-to-use, employee-friendly interface. From onboarding to up-skilling and shift planning to vacation requests, Flip gives employees instant and equal access to the company information, services, and opportunities relevant to them. Flip is trusted by the world’s top companies, including Bosch, McDonald’s Germany, Porsche, and MAHLE. About Work Networks With a focus on fostering stronger connections among teams, Work Networks believes that a great digital employee experience should enhance actual employee experiences, driving smarter and more connected ways of working. Work Networks is a leading reseller and service partner for digital employee experience, intranet, and internal communications platforms, connecting organisations from HQ to the frontline. Specialising in the selection, implementation, and optimisation of secure, efficient communication and collaboration tools, Work Networks enables AI-driven collaboration and staff engagement accessible from any device. Visit www.worknetworks.co.uk to learn more.

title: Qorvo Transforms Enterprise Wi-Fi Access Points into Scalable UWB RTLS Infrastructure
summary: Qorvo® (Nasdaq: QRVO), a leading global provider of connectivity and power solutions, today announced a major step forward in making Ultra-Wideband (UWB) real-time location systems (RTLS) deployable at enterprise scale. By combining industry standards including FiRa and Omlox with integration into Wi-Fi enterprise access points (EAPs), Qorvo enables precise, real-time location services without the need for dedicated RTLS infrastructure.
body_text: Download full size image GREENSBORO, N.C., May 18, 2026 – Qorvo® (Nasdaq: QRVO), a leading global provider of connectivity and power solutions, today announced a major step forward in making Ultra-Wideband (UWB) real-time location systems (RTLS) deployable at enterprise scale. By combining industry standards including FiRa and Omlox with integration into Wi-Fi enterprise access points (EAPs), Qorvo enables precise, real-time location services without the need for dedicated RTLS infrastructure. Qorvo addresses key barriers to RTLS adoption, including fragmented systems and the cost and complexity of dedicated anchor networks. By embedding UWB into enterprise Wi-Fi infrastructure, Qorvo enables location services to scale using existing access points and workflows. With over a decade of UWB innovation, the company provides a proven RTLS foundation deployed across healthcare, mining, logistics and automotive manufacturing environments. “Real-time location has long been limited by infrastructure cost and lack of interoperability,” said Alexis Bizalion, Director of Product Marketing & Enablement at Qorvo. “By bringing standards-based UWB into enterprise Wi-Fi access points, we’re making real-time location a native capability of the network. We’re excited to enable OEMs, system integrators and solution providers to build and deploy RTLS solutions with greater flexibility, lower cost and reduced integration risk.” A key differentiator is Qorvo’s collaboration with leading enterprise Wi-Fi providers to integrate UWB into access points, transforming Wi-Fi infrastructure into a dual-purpose platform for both connectivity and location services while reducing deployment cost and time to market. The company has achieved multiple industry-first UWB milestones, including: FiRa-compliant RTLS deployments on EAPs in healthcare and logistics Omlox-compliant RTLS deployments on EAPs in automotive manufacturing Combined support of FiRa and Omlox standards within enterprise Wi-Fi infrastructure for interoperable RTLS deployments At the core of this ecosystem is Qorvo’s new QPK3000 module, designed for tags and end devices. It enables interoperable UWB functionality across EAPs, dedicated anchors and other UWB-enabled infrastructure, simplifying development while ensuring compatibility across FiRa- and Omlox-based systems. Qorvo recently showcased the QPK3000 and its RTLS ecosystem approach at the Wi-Fi NOW UWB Global Summit in Mountain View, CA, highlighting how standards-based UWB is enabling scalable, interoperable RTLS deployments. For more information on UWB RTLS, visit Qorvo’s Real-Time Location Systems (RTLS) page . About Qorvo Qorvo (Nasdaq: QRVO) supplies innovative semiconductor solutions that make a better world possible. We combine product and technology leadership, systems-level expertise and global manufacturing scale to quickly solve our customers’ most complex technical challenges. Qorvo serves diverse high-growth segments of large global markets, including automotive, consumer, defense & aerospace, industrial & enterprise, infrastructure and mobile. Visit www.qorvo.com to learn how our diverse and innovative team is helping connect, protect and power our planet.
